issue: Can a tribal officer detain a non-Indian on fee land on reasonable suspicion, or must the officer have probable cause?

sides.position: Tribal officers need probable cause ("probable-cause-plus") to investigate or detain a non-Indian for misconduct on fee land within a reservation.
cases: United States v. Joshua Cooley, 947 F.3d 1215 (9th Cir. 2020)

sides.position: Tribal officers may act on reasonable suspicion when investigating non-Indian misconduct on fee land, as the opposing circuit view identified in the dissent.
cases: Jones (cited in the excerpt without a citation or circuit)

this_court: The panel's probable-cause-plus rule, which the dissent criticizes; the excerpt does not show the court's final resolution.
